Returns each profile in full, so no follow-up call is needed to describe one. A profile the user built on the machine appears with its documentation fields null; a profile this server documents that is not currently loaded appears with onMachine false. If the machine cannot be reached the bundled documentation is returned instead, and 'source' and 'note' say so.

description: Get everything known about one brew profile: the machine's own definition of it — brew temperature, the phases it runs with their targets and stop conditions, and the recipe it was written around — plus this server's prose documentation when it has any, whether the profile is on the machine, and the id select_profile takes. This is the right tool for 'what does this profile actually do', including a profile the user built themselves. The definition comes back in the machine's own wire format, so it can be edited and handed to upload_profile. Accepts a documented id, a machine profile id, or the profile's name. Call list_profiles first if you do not already have one. Firmware that predates the machine's per-profile export answers with the documentation alone and says so.

profile_id.description: Id, machine profile id, or name of a profile as listed by list_profiles, e.g. "zer0".

name: get_profile_info

basketNotes.description: Basket and dose notes for this profile, when documented

globalStopConditions.description: What ends the shot regardless of which phase is running: time, weight, waterPumped, switchToManualPressureCtrl, switchToManuaFlowCtrl. `time` is MILLISECONDS, `weight` grams. Null when the profile carries none. Upstream misspells the flow-control flag as switchToManuaFlowCtrl; it is passed through unchanged so a profile can be uploaded back.

name.description: Profile name as stored on the machine

phases.description: Phases in the order the machine runs them. Each has a `type` ("FLOW", "PRESSURE", "MANUAL"), a `target` ramp whose `end` is bar for a PRESSURE phase and ml/s for a FLOW phase, `time` in MILLISECONDS, and a `curve` from "EASE_IN_OUT", "EASE_IN", "EASE_OUT", "LINEAR", "INSTANT". `stopConditions` are drawn from time, pressureAbove, pressureBelow, flowAbove, flowBelow, weight, waterPumpedInPhase, and their `time` is milliseconds too. This is the machine's own wire format, so it can be edited and passed straight back to upload_profile.

recipe.description: The dose and yield the profile was written around, in grams; null when it carries none

waterTemperature.description: Brew temperature the profile asks for, in real degrees Celsius — NOT the scaled-by-10 form the shot time-series uses. 93 means 93°C.

definition.description: The profile as the machine itself stores it: brew temperature, phases with their targets and stop conditions, recipe, and what ends the shot. This is the machine's own wire format — milliseconds, real degrees Celsius — so it can be edited and handed straight to upload_profile. Null when the profile is not on the machine, or when the machine did not serve one; definitionNote says which.

title: Get brew profile details

description: Read the machine's configuration: boiler and steam setpoints, temperature offset, scale and predictive-stop settings, and whatever else this firmware exposes. Useful as dial-in context — a brew temperature that never matches the profile usually shows up here as an offset rather than in the shot data. The fields are whatever the machine sends, so treat unfamiliar names as firmware-specific.
name: get_machine_settings
title: Get machine settings

description: Read the service history the machine tracks for itself: when it last recorded a descale and a backflush, and how many shots it has pulled since each. Reach for it when the shot data points at the machine rather than the coffee — scale build-up shows up as flow that will not match the profile's targets and a brew temperature that will not hold, at a grind setting that used to work. The machine records a descale at 50% of the descale cycle and a backflush once pressure holds above 10 bar in flush mode for more than two seconds, so a service done by hand is not in these numbers, and the shot counters only count shots that ran 5 seconds or longer. Older firmware does not track any of this and says so.
name: get_maintenance_status

services.description: One entry per service this firmware tracks, in the order the machine reported them. Empty means the machine's service log is empty, which is different from the firmware having no service log at all — that comes back as an error result.

lastAt.description: When the machine last recorded this service, as an ISO-8601 UTC instant. Null when it has never recorded one — the machine reports 0 for that, which is not 1 January 1970 — or when the epoch it reported is too early to be a real date, which means its clock was not set at the time.

lastEpochSec.description: The same instant in the machine's own epoch seconds, or null when it has never recorded this service.

service.description: Which service this is, in the machine's own naming: "descale" or "backflush" on current firmware.

shotsSince.description: Shots recorded since that service. Only shots that ran long enough for the machine to record them — 5 seconds — are counted, so flushes and aborted pulls are not in this number. Null when this firmware reports no counter for the service.

title: Get machine service history

description: Switch the machine to a different brew profile. This changes the machine, so confirm the profile with the user before calling it — do not select one on your own initiative from dial-in advice. Takes the id from list_profiles (either the documented id or the machineProfileId). The profile must already be on the machine; this cannot create one. Refuses unless this server has an authorization server configured, since an unauthenticated server exposed over a tunnel would let anyone reach it.

profile_id.description: Id of the profile to select, as listed by list_profiles — either its documented id ("zer0") or its machineProfileId ("15").

name: select_profile
title: Select brew profile

description: Save a new brew profile to the machine. This creates something the user will see on the machine's own screen, so before calling it, show them the whole profile you intend to write — name, brew temperature, and every phase's target and stop conditions — and get an explicit yes. Do not upload a profile you invented while giving dial-in advice. It creates and never updates: the machine assigns a fresh id and ignores any id you send, so calling this twice leaves two profiles, and this server deliberately will not retry it for you — if a call fails without a clear answer, call list_profiles to see whether it landed before trying again. The reliable way to build one is to take a profile that already works, change only what you mean to change, and give it a new name; get_profile_info's `definition` field is exactly this shape. Uploading does not load the profile — call select_profile afterwards, again with the user's agreement. Times are in milliseconds and temperatures in degrees Celsius; these are NOT the x10-scaled values shot datapoints use. Refuses unless this server has an authorization server configured, since an unauthenticated server exposed over a tunnel would let anyone reach it.

profile.description: The profile to save. Do not include an id — the machine assigns a fresh one and ignores any id sent, and passing one is rejected here so a copied profile cannot be mistaken for an edit of the original.

globalStopConditions.description: What ends the whole shot, whichever phase is running.

switchToManuaFlowCtrl.description: Switch to manual flow control instead of stopping. Spelled exactly as the firmware spells it, with one 'l' in 'Manua' — that misspelling is the machine's wire format, not a typo here.

switchToManualPressureCtrl.description: Switch to manual pressure control instead of stopping.

time.description: Stop the shot after this long, in MILLISECONDS (40000 = 40 seconds).

waterPumped.description: Stop once this many millilitres have been pumped.

weight.description: Stop once the scale reads this many grams — the usual way to end a shot on a machine with scales.

name.description: Name the profile appears under on the machine. Give a copy a distinct name — the machine does not enforce unique names, and two profiles called the same thing are indistinguishable on its screen.

phases.description: The phases the shot runs, in order. The machine requires at least one.

name.description: Label shown on the machine, e.g. "Preinfusion".

restriction.description: Flow restriction for the phase; 0 is unrestricted. The machine's documentation does not state its unit, so leave it at 0 unless copying a profile that sets it.

skip.description: True to keep the phase in the profile but not run it.

stopConditions.description: What ends this phase. Omit only for a final phase meant to run until a global stop condition fires — a phase with neither runs until the brew switch is released.

flowAbove.description: End the phase once pump flow rises above this, in ml/s.

flowBelow.description: End the phase once pump flow falls below this, in ml/s.

pressureAbove.description: End the phase once group pressure rises above this, in bar.

pressureBelow.description: End the phase once group pressure falls below this, in bar.

time.description: End the phase after this long, in MILLISECONDS (10000 = 10 seconds).

waterPumpedInPhase.description: End the phase once this many millilitres have been pumped during it. The machine's documentation does not state the unit; millilitres is inferred from the flow units.

weight.description: End the phase once the scale reads this many grams.

target.description: Where the phase drives pressure or flow to, and how fast. Required for a FLOW or PRESSURE phase.

curve.description: How the target moves from start to end over `time`. Omit for the machine's default; INSTANT steps straight to `end`.

end.description: Value to arrive at: bar for a PRESSURE phase, ml/s for a FLOW phase. Real units — 9 means 9 bar, not the x10-scaled 90 a shot's pressure datapoint reports.

start.description: Value to start from, same units as `end`. Omit to continue from where the previous phase ended.

time.description: How long the move from start to end takes, in MILLISECONDS (5000 = 5 seconds). Omit or 0 to step straight to `end`.

volume.description: Optional millilitre budget for the transition. Leave unset unless copying a profile that uses it.

type.description: What the phase controls: PRESSURE holds a pressure target, FLOW holds a flow target, MANUAL hands control to the machine's own sliders.

waterTemperature.description: Per-phase brew temperature override, in degrees Celsius. Omit to use the profile's own waterTemperature.

recipe.description: Dose and yield the profile is written for. Informational.

ratio.description: Yield divided by dose; 2 means 1:2. Informational — the machine does not enforce it.

waterTemperature.description: Brew temperature in degrees Celsius, e.g. 93. Real degrees — not the x10-scaled 930 a shot's temperature datapoint reports. Required here even though the machine would default it to 0, because a profile that brews at 0°C is not a profile.

name: upload_profile

machineProfileId.description: Id the machine assigned the new profile — the value select_profile takes. Null when the machine saved the profile but its answer carried no id; call list_profiles to find it in that case.

name.description: Name the profile was saved under.

Optionally compares two shots side by side — the user can also click 'Compare previous' in the graph to load the prior shot without a new tool call.

compare_shot_id.description: Optional id of a second shot to overlay on the same axes for comparison.

shot_id.description: Id of the shot to visualize, e.g. "1706547890". Call get_latest_shot_id to obtain the most recent one.

title: View shot graph
